title: NOIR — The Nishidak Broadcast
subtitle: A visual treatment for the 30:22 master screenplay
look: Monsoon Bengal in restrained monochrome; phosphor amber and red; a sterile white corridor at the hinge.
studio_handoff: The shot prompts are designed for local image generation in Imagination Studio or another image tool. Existing stills are visual references, not locked frames.

shots.title: The mark in the glass
shots.movement: Hold; the droplet trembles once and falls
shots.story: A nearly black CRT. A thin amber ring and one suspended black drop are just visible. The first ripple disappears before the audience can decide what it means.
shots.text: MAY 14, 1994 · DO NOT ANSWER A FAMILIAR VOICE AFTER MIDNIGHT.
shots.sound: Low electrical presence; let the silence around it stay audible.
shots.prompt: A restrained 1990s CRT close-wide frame, almost black. One fine amber circular aperture above a single glossy black droplet and a delicate water ripple. Symmetrical, minimal, analog texture, subtle scanlines. Hold the image in darkness; no words or logos. 4:3 picture inside a black 16:9 matte.

shots.title: The unlisted transmission
shots.movement: Slow signal lock; one brief tracking slip
shots.story: A calm station slate resolves out of snow. Identification arrives first; the warning follows after a beat.
shots.sound: Soft carrier hum; no stinger on the warning.
shots.prompt: A sober 1994 Bengali public television emergency broadcast slate seen through a curved CRT, dark navy-black glass, a small phosphor amber spiral symbol, restrained green station data, one narrow muted-red alert band. Leave generous empty space for legible type to be added in post. No invented garbled lettering, no contemporary interface.

shots.title: The house listens back
shots.frame: Extreme wide; house small in frame
shots.story: A lonely two-storey Bengal house in flat wet fields. One shutter is slightly open. A single banana leaf turns against the wind.
shots.sound: Monsoon wind held low beneath the drone.
shots.prompt: Wide 4:3 archival frame of a solitary two-storey rural Bengal house in waterlogged fields at night, banana plants and distant palms, damp plaster, one upstairs shutter open a few inches. Keep the house small in a large empty landscape. Restrained near-monochrome, faint warm window light, 1990s CRT grain; no text.

shots.title: Bimal chooses to go
shots.movement: Static; netting drifts after he passes
shots.story: Bimal sits listening. He checks the dark doorway, puts on his shoes, pauses at the threshold, then steps outside. His decision is small and deliberate.
shots.text: RULE 01 · DO NOT FOLLOW A VOICE YOU CANNOT PLACE.
shots.sound: A faint tonal shift suggests a familiar call; no clear voice.
shots.prompt: A quiet, human-scale bedroom in an old rural Bengal house at night. Bimal Babu, an ordinary tired clerk in rumpled cotton work clothes, sits at the edge of a wooden bed beneath a sheer mosquito net, listening toward a dark open window. Profile medium-wide composition; he is alert but not terrified. Damp lime plaster, kerosene-lamp warmth, subtle 1990s film grain, no supernatural creature, no text.

shots.title: The pump makes a pool
shots.movement: Slow push toward the dark surface
shots.story: The handpump moves once by itself. Black liquid spreads where water should soak in. Bimal marks the edge with a stone; the stone later appears beneath the surface.
shots.text: No new card. Let the image hold.
shots.sound: The drone thins into an uneasy near-silence.
shots.prompt: Low, patient 4:3 frame of an old rusted cast-iron handpump in a Bengal courtyard after rain. A small amount of glossy black liquid gathers beneath the spout and forms a clean circular pool in red earth. The pump is still; no gore or fantasy glow. Dark banana leaves, distant house, restrained highlights, 1990s analog film texture.

shots.title: A cat, then a tower
shots.frame: Long lens; fence across lower third
shots.movement: Locked; the neck extends in two slow stages
shots.story: A small black cat sits deadpan on the bamboo rail. Give the ordinary silhouette time to register. Its neck then rises beyond the frame while its body remains still.
shots.sound: The score gains weight without accelerating the cut.
shots.prompt: A gaunt black rural tomcat sits motionless on a split-bamboo fence at night, small against a Bengal courtyard and a low monsoon sky. Keep the animal almost ordinary and faintly absurd. Long-lens 4:3 composition with negative space above for a later neck-extension effect; monochrome CRT archive texture, no giant eye yet, no text.

shots.title: The sky looks down
shots.frame: Low angle, cat and sky share axis
shots.movement: Slow tilt up; stop when the eye meets lens
shots.story: The cloud cover opens around a colossal eye. It does not hunt; it simply settles its gaze on Bimal. The prologue's circle returns in a new scale.
shots.text: Let the visual rhyme carry the beat.
shots.sound: One broad swell; no impact hit.
shots.prompt: A colossal, still eye emerging slowly from bruised monsoon clouds above a Bengal bamboo fence. A long-necked black cat anchors the eye to the ground. Near-monochrome storm palette with one restrained crimson iris and small sulfur-yellow cat eyes. Cosmic scale but composed and quiet, 4:3 archival frame, no lettering.

shots.title: The courtyard tips away
shots.frame: High angle into a circular void
shots.movement: Bimal falls backward; camera remains with him
shots.story: A crack reaches Bimal's shoe. The earth tilts with terrible calm. He reaches for the fence and misses. The pool becomes a dark opening; the world drains to one pale point.
shots.text: No warning card during the fall.
shots.sound: Follow the score's natural drop; avoid added impacts.
shots.prompt: A small human silhouette falling backward into a vast black circular abyss, fragments of a Bengal courtyard and a few horizontal CRT scanlines receding above him. Preserve clear negative space and a strong 4:3 composition. Slow, weightless, restrained monochrome, no spiral tunnel, no extra characters, no text.

shots.title: A clean, quiet place
shots.story: Bimal stands in a spotless fluorescent corridor. He checks his hands and clothes, then walks toward the EXIT 8 sign. The yellow tactile strip is the only color.
shots.prompt: A sterile, empty underground corridor with white square tiles, cool fluorescent ceiling lights, a single yellow tactile strip, deep one-point perspective. Bimal Babu, seen from behind in rumpled work clothes, stands small in the frame. Near-monochrome, crisp and quiet, no other person, no glitch, no extra signage beyond EXIT 8.

shots.title: The man between the lights
shots.frame: Long shot, centered figure; then eye detail
shots.movement: Locked; approach advances only between flickers
shots.story: A suited man stands on the strip with an empty briefcase. Bimal tests the flicker pattern, learns the corridor's rhythm, then sees the broadcast spiral reflected in the man's eye.
shots.text: IF YOU NOTICE A CHANGE, TURN BACK. / IF NOTHING HAS CHANGED, KEEP WALKING.
shots.prompt: A pale, ordinary middle-aged man in a dark grey suit stands motionless on the yellow tactile strip of a clean white-tiled underground corridor, holding a closed briefcase. Symmetrical long shot, fluorescent stillness, no horror makeup. A subtle CRT spiral reflection in one eye for a later close-up. Restrained, clinical, no text.

shots.title: The circle without the drop
shots.movement: Static hold; then cut to black
shots.story: The red playhead reaches the end. The amber mark from the opening returns alone. This time there is no droplet beneath it.
shots.text: No title card. End on black.
shots.sound: Resolve toward silence; hold four seconds.
shots.prompt: The same nearly black CRT composition as the opening: a thin amber circular mark centered in deep black. No droplet, no ripple, no text. Fine scanlines and faint glass curvature. Hold still and let the image fade to absolute black.

rendered_preview.title: Shot 30: Small violet-purple neon LED portal outside the doorway
rendered_preview.story: Above the still courtyard, clouds drift slowly across the sky. The compact black portal pulses with a glossy violet-purple rim: fast charged particles race around it, leaving a soft radiation halo. The image stays mostly steady and natural, with only one brief, restrained tape disturbance. Bimal approaches with a slow, wary gait; at the rim his footing slips, he skids forward, then falls into the opening. The cat and celestial Trinetra appear later, not in this passage.

rendered_preview.status: Five-second compositor preview for review; not a rendered section of the complete 30:22 master.
